update.problem_description:
Perform dimensional analysis for laser-melted liquid metal to derive the dimensionless form of the keyhole depth (denoted as e*). 
This analysis uses ONLY the following 7 physical quantities as input parameters: 
the material density (ρ), the temperature difference between melting temperature and ambient temperature (Tl − T0), the laser beam radius (r0), and the thermal diffusivity (α), the effective laser power (ηP), the heat capacity (cp), the laser scan speed (Vs).
update.analyzed_output_reasoning: The target output e* is the dimensionless keyhole depth (keyhole depth normalized by a length scale such as the laser radius r0) and is therefore dimensionless. It is formed from the listed inputs (density, temperature difference, beam radius, thermal diffusivity, effective laser power, specific heat, and scan speed) via nondimensional combinations (e.g., Buckingham Pi).

dimension_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The target output e* is the dimensionless keyhole depth (keyhole depth normalized by a length scale such as the laser radius r0) and is therefore dimensionless. It is formed from the listed inputs (density, temperature difference, beam radius, thermal diffusivity, effective laser power, specific heat, and scan speed) via nondimensional combinations (e.g., Buckingham Pi).

variables.physical_definition: Material mass density (mass per unit volume of the molten metal)
Temperature difference between the material melting temperature and ambient/reference temperature
Laser beam radius (characteristic length scale of the irradiated spot)
Thermal diffusivity of the material (rate of thermal diffusion)
Effective laser power (laser power multiplied by optical/absorption efficiency)
Specific heat capacity (heat capacity per unit mass of the material)
Laser scan speed (velocity of the laser relative to the material)

workflow_plan.rationale: A single-mechanism (single_regime_adaptive) workflow is appropriate because the prompt does not request multiple mechanisms or automatic mechanism screening. First-kind similarity (dependent-variable not scaled) is the default; optimize_output is set to false. With 90 samples the Kraskov mutual-information estimator is preferred (mi_param k=6). The problem specifies three independent base-Pi generators, so we keep start_count=1 and allow the runtime to determine the number of dominant Pi groups numerically. Both fixed_in_power and fixed_out_power dictionaries are present (empty here because no explicit exponent constraints were given) to respect the protocol. Other numeric thresholds (minimum samples, sparsification, MI screening tolerances) use conservative defaults suitable for the dataset size.

update.final_report:
- e* ∝ ηP^{2/3}/(ρ^{2/3}ΔT^{2/3} r0 α^{1/3} c_p^{2/3} V_s^{1/3}). It quantifies the competition of delivered laser energy (heating) vs thermal sinks—melting enthalpy (ρ c_p ΔT), diffusion (α) and scan advection (V_s); keyhole depth rises ~P^{2/3}. Validation: no exact classical identity.  
- RAG grounding: Closest match is the Keyhole number Ke = ηP/(π ρ c_p ΔT √(α V_s r0^3)); not algebraically equivalent (contextual only). Ke likewise balances power against conductive/advective removal and predicts keyhole aspect ratio/stability (Gan et al., 2021).
